content: The provided text is a detailed pharmacological interaction guide, primarily focusing on the effects of co-administration of cobicistat and other drugs. 1. Cobicistat and Cenobamate: Adjust the dose of cenobamate as needed when co-administered with cobicistat to avoid potential toxicity. 2. Cobicistat with Cobicistat or Ceritinib: These combinations can significantly increase toxicity due to inhibition of CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. There is also a risk of QT prolongation. 3. Cobicistat and Chloramphenicol: Chloramphenicol increases cobicistat levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 4. Cobicistat and Chlordiazepoxide: Cobicistat increases chlordiazepoxide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Cobicistat and Ciclesonide (Inhaled): Cobicistat increases ciclesonide levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Cobicistat and Cilostazol: Cobicistat increases cilostazol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce cilostazol dose to 50 mg twice daily and monitor for adverse effects. 7. Cobicistat and Citalopram: Cobicistat increases citalopram levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely due to the risk of QT prolongation. 8. Cobicistat and Clarithromycin: Clarithromycin increases cobicistat levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, and vice versa. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Consider alternative antibiotics when cobicistat is co-administered with atazanavir or darunavir. 9. Cobicistat and Clomipramine: Cobicistat increases clomipramine levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Carefully titrate the antidepressant dose to the desired effect, using the lowest feasible dose, and monitor for response. 10. Cobicistat and Clonazepam: Cobicistat increases clonazepam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely, especially when co-administered with anticonvulsants. 11. Cobicistat and Clorazepate: Cobicistat increases clorazepate levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Adjust the clorazepate dose if necessary and monitor closely. 12. Cobicistat and Elvitegravir: Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors like cobicistat increases elvitegravir levels. Avoid or use alternative drugs to prevent loss of therapeutic effect and resistance. 13. Cobicistat and Colchicine: Cobicistat increases colchicine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Co-administration is contraindicated in patients with renal or hepatic impairment due to the risk of serious or life-threatening reactions. Adjust colchicine dosage as needed and refer to prescribing information. 14. Cobicistat and Conivaptan: Conivaptan increases cobicistat levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, and vice versa. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 15. Cobicistat and Cyclophosphamide: Cyclophosphamide increases cobicistat levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitor closely. 16. Cobicistat and Cyclosporine: Cobicistat increases cyclosporine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 17. Cobicistat and Dabigatran: Cobicistat increases dabigatran levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Avoid co-administration if CrCl <30 mL/min for atrial fibrillation or <50 mL/min for DVT/PE treatment. 18. Cobicistat and Dexamethasone: Co-administration with corticosteroids metabolized by CYP3A4 may increase systemic corticosteroid effects, such as Cushing syndrome and adrenal suppression. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 19. Cobicistat and Diazepam: Cobicistat increases diazepam levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. A reduced diazepam dose may be required. Monitor closely for adverse reactions. 20. Cobicistat and Digoxin: Cobicistat increases digoxin levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Measure serum digoxin concentrations before initiating concomitant drugs and adjust the dose by 30-50% or modify dosing frequency. 21. Cobicistat and Diltiazem: Cobicistat increases diltiazem levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Cobicistat and Disopyramide: Cobicistat increases disopyramide levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Clinical monitoring is recommended when co-administered with antiarrhythmics. 23. Cobicistat and Docetaxel: Cobicistat increases docetaxel levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Consider reducing the docetaxel dose by 50% if co-administration cannot be avoided. 24. Cobicistat and Doravirine: Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors like cobicistat may increase doravirine plasma concentrations and toxicities. Monitor closely. 25. Cobicistat and Doxepin: Cobicistat increases doxepin levels via CYP2D6 inhibition. Carefully titrate the antidepressant dose to the desired effect, using the lowest feasible dose, and monitor for response. 26. Cobicistat and Didanosine: Didanosine must be administered on an empty stomach, at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after elvitegravir (administered with food). 27. Cobicistat and Dihydroergotamine: Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of serious or life-threatening reactions, such as acute ergot toxicity characterized by peripheral vasospasm and ischemia. 28. Cobicistat and Deflazacort: Cobicistat increases deflazacort levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Decrease the deflazacort dose to one-third of the recommended dose if co-administered with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 29. Cobicistat and Desipramine: Cobicistat increases desipramine levels via CYP2D6 inhibition. Carefully titrate the antidepressant dose to the desired effect, using the lowest feasible dose, and monitor for response. 30. Cobicistat and Dexlansoprazole: Cobicistat increases dexlansoprazole levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Cobicistat and Darunavir: Cobicistat increases darunavir levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, and vice versa. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 32. Cobicistat and Dasatinib: Cobicistat increases dasatinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Dosage adjustment may be necessary. Refer to prescribing information for dosing instructions. 33. Cobicistat and Daridorexant: Cobicistat increases daridorexant levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 34. Cobicistat and Darifenacin: Cobicistat increases darifenacin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 35. Cobicistat and Darolutamide: Cobicistat increases darolutamide levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Adjust therapy and monitor closely.
